calls.head: Depth vs. star power
calls.body: On depth, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Columbus is near the bottom. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.

calls.head: The Islanders’ edge in shots from in close
calls.body: The Islanders are around the middle of the league for shots from in close, and the Blue Jackets are one of the worst. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: A hat trick for Schaefer, and the hats come down
paras: Anthony Duclair struck first for the Islanders on the power play late in the first, and Matthew Schaefer extended the lead to 2-0 early in the second. It was a busy third period. Zach Werenski pulled the Blue Jackets within one early in the period, but that was as close as they got. Schaefer scored again later in the period to make it 3-1 for the Islanders, and the goal stood after the Jackets challenged for goalie interference. Tony DeAngelo stretched the lead to 4-1 just under five minutes later, and Schaefer completed his hat trick into the empty net with just under four minutes left.
The Islanders drove the play, outshooting the Blue Jackets 41-29, and the scoreboard caught up. Ilya Sorokin made 28 saves for the Islanders, and Cam Talbot stopped 36 of 40 at the other end.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Islanders moved to 10-6-4, fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Blue Jackets fell to 7-12-0, still last in the Metropolitan.
